# Template: distribution_curve
A probability distribution curve — a normal (Gaussian) bell curve, or a right- or left-skewed curve — with a dashed mean guide, optional tick marks at ±1 and ±2 standard deviations, and an optional shaded tail (upper, lower, or both/two-sided) with a percentage or probability label. Choose this scene for ANY request about a normal distribution, bell curve, probability distribution, standard deviation, z-score, p-value, a statistical significance threshold, a critical region, a skewed distribution, or shading the tail(s) of a distribution. The shade boundaries take typed numbers or a code element's variable via a "{id.var}" token — a critical value or z-score the script computed — and until it has run the curve draws with the boundary at ±1σ, so the shade beats exist from the first frame. TYPE the shade's `label` and `side` by hand: a token can supply a number, never a mode or a caption.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "kind": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "normal",
    "right_skew",
    "left_skew"
   ],
   "description": "Default \"normal\"."
  },
  "mean_label": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Default \"μ\"."
  },
  "sd_label": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Default \"σ\"."
  },
  "shade": {
   "type": "object",
   "properties": {
    "from": {
     "oneOf": [
      {
       "type": "number",
       "description": "Standard deviations from the mean where shading starts, e.g. 1.96."
      },
      {
       "type": "string",
       "pattern": "^\\{[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*\\}$"
      }
     ]
    },
    "to": {
     "oneOf": [
      {
       "type": "number",
       "description": "Standard deviations from the mean where shading ends (default: the edge of the curve)."
      },
      {
       "type": "string",
       "pattern": "^\\{[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*\\}$"
      }
     ]
    },
    "side": {
     "type": "string",
     "enum": [
      "upper",
      "lower",
      "two"
     ],
     "description": "upper shades the right tail from `from` SDs upward; lower shades the left tail; two shades both tails symmetrically (default upper)."
    },
    "label": {
     "type": "string",
     "description": "e.g. \"2.5%\"."
    }
   }
  },
  "show_sd_ticks": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Tick marks at ±1σ and ±2σ (default true)."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- axis: the horizontal value axis
- curve: the sampled distribution curve
- shade: the shaded tail region, present when `shade` is set
- shade2: the second (mirrored) shaded tail, present only when shade.side is "two"
- shade_label: the shaded region's label, present when `shade` is set
- mean_line: dashed guide at the mean, with its label
- sd_tick_<i>: tick mark at ±1σ/±2σ, present when show_sd_ticks
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Explain a p-value cutoff of 0.05, two-sided, with a normal curve." → params: {"shade":{"from":1.96,"side":"two","label":"2.5% each tail"},"title":"Two-sided significance at α = 0.05"}
Request: "Draw a right-skewed distribution." → params: {"kind":"right_skew"}

In YAML: `template: distribution_curve` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
